subproblems.title: Good radius: a level in (ρ, ρ') with a prescribed a.e. property, a μ-null sphere and a Markov bound
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on (the Borel sets of) ℝ^P, y ∈ ℝ^P, and ρ < ρ' real numbers. Let g : ℝ → [0, ∞] be L¹-a.e. measurable (L¹ = Lebesgue measure on ℝ), let I ∈ [0, ∞] with ∫_ℝ g dL¹ ≤ I (lower Lebesgue integral), and let p be a property of real numbers holding for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ. Assume μ(B̄_{ρ'}(y)) < ∞. Then there is t ∈ ℝ with ρ < t < ρ' such that p(t) holds, μ(∂B_t(y)) = 0, where ∂B_t(y) = {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x − y| = t} (Metric.sphere y t), and g(t) ≤ (2/(ρ' − ρ))·I, the product being computed in [0, ∞] as ENNReal.ofReal(2/(ρ' − ρ))·I.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (ρ ρ' : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (I : ℝ≥0∞) (p : ℝ → Prop), ρ < ρ' → μ (closedBall y ρ') ≠ ∞ → AEMeasurable g → ∫⁻ t, g t ≤ I → (∀ᵐ t, p t) → ∃ t : ℝ, ρ < t ∧ t < ρ' ∧ p t ∧ μ (sphere y t) = 0 ∧ g t ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 / (ρ' - ρ)) * I
subproblems.natural_proof:
This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmb_glc_good_radius (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.level_cut-a1.good_radius-a1, accepted, candidate cbce4763), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. In the selected theorem it carries steps 4–5 of the supplied proof: it chooses ρ in (0, s) outside the null set N and outside the non-differentiability set of G = F^{1/n}, with μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0 and G′(ρ) at most twice its average (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2 (3)). It is applied with y := x₁, ρ := 0, ρ′ := s, g := 1_{(0,s)}·ofReal(G′), I := ofReal(G(s) − G(0)), p(t) := (t ∉ N ∧ G differentiable at t). Its accepted proof follows verbatim.

Source: step 4 of the parent proof (choice of t), which follows Simon 7.2.4, displays (3)–(5) (chapter-07.txt lines 193–204: the level α is chosen by the slicing theory so that the slice is good and M(T_j⌞∂W_α) = 0), with the factor-2 averaging selection of Simon Ch. 2, 6.7(1) (chapter-02.txt lines 1512–1530). The parent's three sets E₁ (slice property), E₂ (null spheres) and E₃ (Markov bound) are abstracted here into p, μ and (g, I). Notation: J := (ρ, ρ'), δ := ρ' − ρ > 0, c := ofReal(2/δ) ∈ [0, ∞]; L¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ, used as an outer measure (monotone and countably subadditive on arbitrary subsets of ℝ); ∂B_s := ∂B_s(y) = {x : |x − y| = s}, B̄_s := B̄_s(y).
1. Facts about c. Since 2/δ > 0 we have c ≠ 0, and c ≠ ∞ because ofReal is finite. Moreover c⁻¹ = ofReal((2/δ)⁻¹) = ofReal(δ/2) (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos and (2/δ)⁻¹ = δ/2).
2. The exceptional set of p. Let N₁ := {t ∈ ℝ : p(t) fails}. Since p holds L¹-a.e., L¹(N₁) = 0 (ae_iff).
3. Charged spheres. Let ν := μ⌞B̄_{ρ'}, i.e. ν(A) = μ(A ∩ B̄_{ρ'}) for Borel A. Then ν(ℝ^P) = μ(B̄_{ρ'}) < ∞, so ν is a finite (hence s-finite) measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). The spheres ∂B_s, s ∈ ℝ, are closed, hence Borel, and pairwise disjoint: if x ∈ ∂B_s ∩ ∂B_{s'} then s = |x − y| = s'. For an s-finite measure only countably many members of a pairwise disjoint family of measurable sets have positive measure (Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion). Hence N₂ := {s ∈ ℝ : 0 < ν(∂B_s)} is countable, and L¹(N₂) = 0 because L¹ has no atoms (Set.Countable.measure_zero). Moreover, if s ≤ ρ' then ∂B_s ⊆ B̄_s ⊆ B̄_{ρ'}, so ν(∂B_s) = μ(∂B_s ∩ B̄_{ρ'}) = μ(∂B_s) (Measure.restrict_apply for the closed set ∂B_s).
4. The Markov set. Let N₃ := {t ∈ ℝ : c·I < g(t)}. We show L¹(N₃) ≤ ofReal(δ/2) by cases on I.
 (a) I = 0. Then ∫ g dL¹ ≤ 0, so ∫ g dL¹ = 0, and since g is a.e.-measurable, g = 0 L¹-a.e. (lintegral_eq_zero_iff'). As c·I = 0, every t ∈ N₃ has g(t) > 0, so N₃ ⊆ {t : g(t) ≠ 0}, an L¹-null set; hence L¹(N₃) = 0 ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
 (b) I = ∞. Since c ≠ 0, c·I = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_top), and no t satisfies ∞ < g(t). So N₃ = ∅ and L¹(N₃) = 0 ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
 (c) I ≠ 0 and I ≠ ∞. Put ε := c·I; then ε ≠ 0 (as c ≠ 0 and I ≠ 0) and ε ≠ ∞ (as c ≠ ∞ and I ≠ ∞). Since N₃ ⊆ {t : ε ≤ g(t)}, Markov's inequality for the a.e.-measurable g (meas_ge_le_lintegral_div) gives L¹(N₃) ≤ L¹({ε ≤ g}) ≤ (∫ g dL¹)/ε ≤ I/(c·I). Finally I/(c·I) = (c·I)⁻¹·I = c⁻¹·(I⁻¹·I) = c⁻¹ (ENNReal.mul_inv, using c ≠ 0 and c ≠ ∞, and I⁻¹·I = 1 since I ≠ 0, ∞), and c⁻¹ = ofReal(δ/2) by step 1. Hence L¹(N₃) ≤ ofReal(δ/2).
5. Covering. Suppose, for a contradiction, that no t satisfies ρ < t < ρ', p(t), μ(∂B_t) = 0 and g(t) ≤ c·I. Then J ⊆ N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃: otherwise take t ∈ J outside N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃. Then p(t) holds (t ∉ N₁); ν(∂B_t) = 0 (t ∉ N₂), hence μ(∂B_t) = ν(∂B_t) = 0 by step 3 because t < ρ'; and g(t) ≤ c·I (t ∉ N₃). So t has all four properties, contradicting the assumption.
6. By monotonicity and subadditivity of L¹ and steps 2–4, ofReal(δ) = L¹(J) ≤ L¹(N₁) + L¹(N₂) + L¹(N₃) ≤ 0 + 0 + ofReal(δ/2) = ofReal(δ/2) (Real.volume_Ioo). Since δ/2 ≥ 0, this gives δ ≤ δ/2 (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff), i.e. δ ≤ 0, contradicting δ > 0.
7. Hence there is t with ρ < t < ρ', p(t), μ(∂B_t(y)) = 0 and g(t) ≤ ofReal(2/(ρ' − ρ))·I. ∎
proof_key_steps: N₁ := {t : ¬p(t)} is L¹-null; N₂ := {s : μ⌞B̄_{ρ'}(y)(∂B_s(y)) > 0} is countable (pairwise disjoint closed spheres, finite measure), hence L¹-null; μ⌞B̄_{ρ'}(y) and μ agree on ∂B_s(y) for s ≤ ρ'.
N₃ := {t : (2/(ρ'−ρ))·I < g(t)} has L¹-measure ≤ (ρ'−ρ)/2: if I = 0 then g = 0 a.e.; if I = ∞ then N₃ = ∅; otherwise Markov's inequality with ε = (2/(ρ'−ρ))·I.
If no good t existed, (ρ, ρ') ⊆ N₁ ∪ N₂ ∪ N₃, so ρ' − ρ ≤ 0 + 0 + (ρ' − ρ)/2, a contradiction.

subproblems.title: Lebesgue's inequality ∫_a^b F′ ≤ F(b) − F(a) for monotone F (lower-integral form)
subproblems.statement: Let F : ℝ → ℝ be monotone (nondecreasing) and a, b ∈ ℝ, and let F′ := deriv F (Mathlib's derivative, equal to 0 at points where F is not differentiable). Then the lower Lebesgue integral over (a, b) with respect to Lebesgue measure satisfies ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(F′(t)) dt ≤ ofReal(F(b) − F(a)), where ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is ENNReal.ofReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (F : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ), Monotone F → ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, ENNReal.ofReal (deriv F t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (F b - F a)
subproblems.natural_proof:
This child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmcs_smi_lintegral_ofReal_deriv_le (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.slicing-a1.mass_integral-a1.lebesgue_deriv-a1, accepted, candidate 6efe397f), reused at its byte-identical frozen type. In the selected theorem it is step 3 of the supplied proof (∫_0^s G′ ≤ G(s) − G(0) for the nondecreasing G = F^{1/n}), applied with F := G, a := 0, b := s. Its accepted Lean proof uses only the frozen imports (the Stieltjes measure of G and Monotone.ae_hasDerivAt), so the DerivIntegrable import mentioned below is not needed. Its accepted proof follows verbatim.

Provenance: Simon Ch. 6, the remark preceding 4.10 (chapter-06.txt lines 1367–1376: an increasing function of t is differentiable for L¹-a.e. t and the integral of its derivative over [a, b] is at most its increment), as used in step 5 of the parent node's proof. This is Lebesgue's theorem for monotone functions (Royden–Fitzpatrick, Real Analysis, 4th ed., §6.2, Corollary 4). The proof below is self-contained. In Mathlib its interval-integral form is MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv together with MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc. Both live in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.DerivIntegrable, which is not in the import closure of the frozen contract. Add `import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntervalIntegral.DerivIntegrable` to the Submission header; accepted solutions in this run add Mathlib imports the same way, and the frozen statement itself elaborates without it. Here deriv F is Mathlib's derivative, which is 0 wherever F is not differentiable.
1. (Empty interval.) If b ≤ a then Ioo a b = ∅ (Set.Ioo_eq_empty). The measure volume.restrict ∅ is 0 (Measure.restrict_empty), so the left side is 0 (lintegral_zero_measure), which is ≤ the right side. Assume from now on a < b.
2. (Nonnegativity.) Because F is monotone, deriv F t ≥ 0 for every t ∈ ℝ (Monotone.deriv_nonneg).
3. (Integrability.) F is monotone on uIcc a b (Monotone.monotoneOn), so deriv F is interval integrable on a..b (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv). Since a ≤ b, this is IntegrableOn (deriv F) (Ioc a b) (intervalIntegrable_iff_integrableOn_Ioc_of_le). Hence IntegrableOn (deriv F) (Ioo a b) (IntegrableOn.mono_set with Ioo_subset_Ioc_self).
4. (Lower integral equals the real integral.) Apply ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal to the measure volume.restrict (Ioo a b), using steps 2 and 3: ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F t) dt = ofReal(∫_{(a,b)} deriv F t dt). Since ofReal is monotone (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal), it suffices to prove ∫_{(a,b)} deriv F ≤ F(b) − F(a).
5. (Conversion to an interval integral.) Lebesgue measure has no atoms, so ∫_{Ioo a b} deriv F = ∫_{Ioc a b} deriv F (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, read right to left). Since a ≤ b, ∫_{Ioc a b} deriv F = ∫_a^b deriv F (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, read right to left).
6. (Lebesgue's bound.) Apply MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc to F, which is monotone on uIcc a b: ∫_a^b deriv F ∈ uIcc 0 (F(b) − F(a)). Since a ≤ b, monotonicity gives F(a) ≤ F(b), so 0 ≤ F(b) − F(a) and uIcc 0 (F(b) − F(a)) = Icc 0 (F(b) − F(a)) (Set.uIcc_of_le). Hence ∫_a^b deriv F ≤ F(b) − F(a), which by steps 4–5 is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: If b ≤ a, the domain Ioo a b is empty and the integral is 0.
deriv F ≥ 0 everywhere (Monotone.deriv_nonneg), and deriv F is integrable on (a, b) (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv, restricted from Ioc to Ioo).
∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F) = ofReal(∫_{(a,b)} deriv F) = ofReal(∫_a^b deriv F) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le).
∫_a^b deriv F ∈ uIcc 0 (F b − F a) = Icc 0 (F b − F a) (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc, F a ≤ F b), so ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal gives the bound.

subproblems.title: Inner-annulus quotients are bounded by the derivative of r ↦ μ(B_r(x₁))
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P (Borel sets), x₁ ∈ ℝ^P, and ρ, d ∈ ℝ with μ(B_ρ(x₁)) < ∞, where B_r(x₁) = ball x₁ r is the open ball. Let F(r) := μ(B_r(x₁)) read as a real number (ENNReal.toReal, which is 0 if the measure is infinite). If F has derivative d at ρ (HasDerivAt F d ρ), then liminf_{h→0, h>0} h⁻¹·μ({x : ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}) ≤ d, where the liminf is taken in [0, ∞] along 𝓝[>] 0 with the factor ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹, and the right side is ENNReal.ofReal d.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (x₁ : Euclid P) (ρ d : ℝ), μ (ball x₁ ρ) ≠ ∞ → HasDerivAt (fun r : ℝ => (μ (ball x₁ r)).toReal) d ρ → liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ {x | ρ - h < dist x x₁ ∧ dist x x₁ < ρ}) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal d
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the supplied proof of the selected theorem. The backward difference quotient of F(r) = μ(B_r(x₁)) controls the measure of thin inner annuli. Simon Ch. 6, proof of 8.2, uses f′(r) for f(r) = M(T⌞B_r(ξ)) in the same way in displays (2)–(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 2338–2357).

Notation: B_r(x₁) = ball x₁ r is the open ball, |x − x₁| = dist x x₁, F(r) := (μ(B_r(x₁))).toReal for r ∈ ℝ, A_h := {x : ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}, ofReal := ENNReal.ofReal. Only the values F(ρ) and F(ρ − h) with h > 0 are used. These are finite measures (step 3(b)), so the convention toReal ∞ = 0 never applies.

1. (Backward difference quotients converge to d.) Since F has derivative d at ρ, t⁻¹·(F(ρ + t) − F(ρ)) → d as t → 0 through negative values, i.e. along 𝓝[<] 0 (Mathlib HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero_left; on ℝ the scalar action • is multiplication). The map h ↦ −h tends from 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[<] 0: it is continuous with −0 = 0, and −h < 0 whenever h > 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff). Compose the two limits and use the identity (−h)⁻¹·(F(ρ + (−h)) − F(ρ)) = h⁻¹·(F(ρ) − F(ρ − h)), valid for every real h. This gives q(h) := h⁻¹·(F(ρ) − F(ρ − h)) → d as h → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 (Filter.Tendsto.congr').

2. (The limit in [0, ∞].) ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is continuous (ENNReal.continuous_ofReal), so ofReal(q(h)) → ofReal(d) along 𝓝[>] 0. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial, hence liminf_{𝓝[>] 0} ofReal(q(h)) = ofReal(d) (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq).

3. (Pointwise comparison.) Fix h > 0.
 (a) A_h ⊆ B_ρ(x₁) ∖ B_{ρ−h}(x₁): if x ∈ A_h then |x − x₁| < ρ, so x ∈ B_ρ(x₁); and x ∉ B_{ρ−h}(x₁), since otherwise |x − x₁| < ρ − h < |x − x₁|.
